resources.string: The harness is a Node.js application. Run it on this phone with Termux, or on a computer, then connect this app to it. You get the same Web UI a desktop browser opens.
Android can host the harness itself inside Termux, a terminal app that ships a Node.js runtime. Install it, paste the two commands below, then tap Check again.
dsh prints a tokenized URL in Termux. Tap Check again, then paste that token.
Found the harness on this phone. Paste the token dsh printed in Termux.
Nothing is listening on 127.0.0.1:%1$d yet. Start dsh in Termux, keep it in the foreground, then check again.
Termux is not installed. Install it from F-Droid or the Play Store, then reopen this screen.
Found the harness on this phone. Connecting\u2026

Use your computer\u2019s LAN address in place of 192.168.1.20 (for example the number `hostname -I` or ipconfig prints). Tap the command to copy it. dsh prints a URL that contains a one-time login token.
Paste the URL dsh printed into the address field below. The app keeps the login cookie, so the token is only needed once per server restart.
Paste the token from the printed URL
No token saved \u2014 paste one if the server asks
Tap to use this address \u00b7 long-press to remove
%1$s will be removed from the recent list.
Address selected. Paste the launch token if you have one, then tap Connect.
The download could not be started.
This download is created inside the page and cannot be saved on the phone.

The harness keeps running on your computer; the phone is a remote control. Traffic is plain HTTP on your local network unless your deployment uses TLS. Never expose dsh directly to the internet \u2014 put a TLS proxy or a VPN in front of it.
No server answered on port %1$d. Check that dsh is running with --host and that both devices share the same network.
Tap an address below, then connect.
Address pasted. Tap Connect to open it.
That address could not be parsed. Use a host or IP, for example 192.168.1.20:3080.
That host name was not found. Use the computer\u2019s IP address instead.
The connection was refused. dsh is probably not listening on this address and port, or a firewall is blocking it.
The connection timed out. Check that the phone and the computer are on the same network.
The page could not be loaded.
The server is running but did not accept this session. Every dsh restart prints a new login URL: paste it again to sign in.
The page renderer stopped. Restarting the view\u2026
No app can open this link.
No file picker is available on this device.
Both devices must be on the same network, dsh must stay running, and the address must include the port.

DeepSeek Harness mobile client %1$s

This is a thin client for the dsh Web UI. The agent, its tools, and your files stay on the machine running dsh; the phone is only the screen.

Open source: github.com/deepseek-harness/deepseek-harness
